item.title: Azuchi Castle Ruins: Nobunaga's Vanished Golden Tower — Guide
item.description: Azuchi Castle was the wonder of its age: the revolutionary fortress-palace Oda Nobunaga raised above Lake Biwa in 1579, its seven-storey tower gilded and painted inside by the era’s finest artists — and it stood barely three years before burning down in the chaos after Nobunaga’s assassination in 1582. What remains is one of Japan’s most evocative ruins: grand stone stairways climbing through cedar woods past the foundation stones of vanished gates and residences to the tower base, where the view over the lake explains at a glance why Nobunaga chose this hill to rule Japan from.

item.title: Gifu Castle: A Mountaintop Castle With Sweeping Valley Views — Guide
item.description: Gifu Castle sits dramatically atop 329-metre Mount Kinka, reached by a ropeway followed by a short walk, and was once the stronghold of the warlord Oda Nobunaga, who launched his campaign to unify Japan from here in the 16th century. Though the current keep is a modern reconstruction, its commanding hilltop position offers sweeping panoramic views over Gifu City, the Nagara River winding below and the surrounding plains, making the journey up as much about the vista as the castle itself.
